Path.doc:
PurePath subclass that can make system calls.

Path represents a filesystem path but unlike PurePath, also offers
methods to do system calls on path objects. Depending on your system,
instantiating a Path will return either a PosixPath or a WindowsPath
object. You can also instantiate a PosixPath or WindowsPath directly,
but cannot instantiate a WindowsPath on a POSIX system or vice versa.

__str__.doc:
Return the string representation of the path, suitable for
passing to system calls.

absolute.doc:
Return an absolute version of this path.  This function works
even if the path doesn't point to anything.

No normalization is done, i.e. all '.' and '..' will be kept along.
Use resolve() to get the canonical path to a file.

as_posix.doc:
Return the string representation of the path with forward (/)
slashes.

as_uri.doc: Return the path as a 'file' URI.

chmod.doc: Change the permissions of the path, like os.chmod().

cwd.doc:
Return a new path pointing to the current working directory
(as returned by os.getcwd()).

expanduser.doc:
Return a new path with expanded ~ and ~user constructs
(as returned by os.path.expanduser)

glob.doc:
Iterate over this subtree and yield all existing files (of any
kind, including directories) matching the given relative pattern.

group.doc: Return the group name of the file gid.

hardlink_to.doc:
Make this path a hard link pointing to the same file as *target*.

Note the order of arguments (self, target) is the reverse of os.link's.

home.doc:
Return a new path pointing to the user's home directory (as
returned by os.path.expanduser('~')).

is_absolute.doc:
True if the path is absolute (has both a root and, if applicable,
a drive).

is_block_device.doc: Whether this path is a block device.

is_char_device.doc: Whether this path is a character device.

is_dir.doc: Whether this path is a directory.

is_fifo.doc: Whether this path is a FIFO.

is_file.doc:
Whether this path is a regular file (also True for symlinks pointing
to regular files).

is_mount.doc: Check if this path is a POSIX mount point

is_relative_to.doc: Return True if the path is relative to another path or False.

is_reserved.doc:
Return True if the path contains one of the special names reserved
by the system, if any.

is_socket.doc: Whether this path is a socket.

is_symlink.doc: Whether this path is a symbolic link.

iterdir.doc:
Iterate over the files in this directory.  Does not yield any
result for the special paths '.' and '..'.

joinpath.doc:
Combine this path with one or several arguments, and return a
new path representing either a subpath (if all arguments are relative
paths) or a totally different path (if one of the arguments is
anchored).

lchmod.doc:
Like chmod(), except if the path points to a symlink, the symlink's
permissions are changed, rather than its target's.

link_to.doc:
Make the target path a hard link pointing to this path.

Note this function does not make this path a hard link to *target*,
despite the implication of the function and argument names. The order
of arguments (target, link) is the reverse of Path.symlink_to, but
matches that of os.link.

Deprecated since Python 3.10 and scheduled for removal in Python 3.12.
Use `hardlink_to()` instead.

lstat.doc:
Like stat(), except if the path points to a symlink, the symlink's
status information is returned, rather than its target's.

match.doc: Return True if this path matches the given pattern.

mkdir.doc: Create a new directory at this given path.

open.doc:
Open the file pointed by this path and return a file object, as
the built-in open() function does.

owner.doc: Return the login name of the file owner.

read_bytes.doc: Open the file in bytes mode, read it, and close the file.

read_text.doc: Open the file in text mode, read it, and close the file.

readlink.doc: Return the path to which the symbolic link points.

relative_to.doc:
Return the relative path to another path identified by the passed
arguments.  If the operation is not possible (because this is not
a subpath of the other path), raise ValueError.

rename.doc:
Rename this path to the target path.

The target path may be absolute or relative. Relative paths are
interpreted relative to the current working directory, *not* the
directory of the Path object.

Returns the new Path instance pointing to the target path.

replace.doc:
Rename this path to the target path, overwriting if that path exists.

The target path may be absolute or relative. Relative paths are
interpreted relative to the current working directory, *not* the
directory of the Path object.

Returns the new Path instance pointing to the target path.

resolve.doc:
Make the path absolute, resolving all symlinks on the way and also
normalizing it (for example turning slashes into backslashes under
Windows).

rglob.doc:
Recursively yield all existing files (of any kind, including
directories) matching the given relative pattern, anywhere in
this subtree.

rmdir.doc: Remove this directory.  The directory must be empty.

samefile.doc:
Return whether other_path is the same or not as this file
(as returned by os.path.samefile()).

stat.doc:
Return the result of the stat() system call on this path, like
os.stat() does.

symlink_to.doc:
Make this path a symlink pointing to the target path.
Note the order of arguments (link, target) is the reverse of os.symlink.

touch.doc: Create this file with the given access mode, if it doesn't exist.

unlink.doc:
Remove this file or link.
If the path is a directory, use rmdir() instead.

with_name.doc: Return a new path with the file name changed.

with_stem.doc: Return a new path with the stem changed.

with_suffix.doc:
Return a new path with the file suffix changed.  If the path
has no suffix, add given suffix.  If the given suffix is an empty
string, remove the suffix from the path.

write_bytes.doc: Open the file in bytes mode, write to it, and close the file.

write_text.doc: Open the file in text mode, write to it, and close the file.

dataclass.signature: (cls=None, /, *, init=True, repr=True, eq=True, order=False, unsafe_hash=False, frozen=False, match_args=True, kw_only=False, slots=False)
dataclass.doc:
Returns the same class as was passed in, with dunder methods
added based on the fields defined in the class.

Examines PEP 526 __annotations__ to determine fields.

If init is true, an __init__() method is added to the class. If
repr is true, a __repr__() method is added. If order is true, rich
comparison dunder methods are added. If unsafe_hash is true, a
__hash__() method function is added. If frozen is true, fields may
not be assigned to after instance creation. If match_args is true,
the __match_args__ tuple is added. If kw_only is true, then by
default all fields are keyword-only. If slots is true, an
__slots__ attribute is added.

field.signature: (*, default=<dataclasses._MISSING_TYPE object at 0x0000021AE37574F0>, default_factory=<dataclasses._MISSING_TYPE object at 0x0000021AE37574F0>, init=True, repr=True, hash=None, compare=True, metadata=None, kw_only=<dataclasses._MISSING_TYPE object at 0x0000021AE37574F0>)
field.doc:
Return an object to identify dataclass fields.

default is the default value of the field.  default_factory is a
0-argument function called to initialize a field's value.  If init
is true, the field will be a parameter to the class's __init__()
function.  If repr is true, the field will be included in the
object's repr().  If hash is true, the field will be included in the
object's hash().  If compare is true, the field will be used in
comparison functions.  metadata, if specified, must be a mapping
which is stored but not otherwise examined by dataclass.  If kw_only
is true, the field will become a keyword-only parameter to
__init__().

It is an error to specify both default and default_factory.
